description: test_chunking_char_count_matches_content_length sums char counts from two threads without a lock
find:
chunks = _service().chunk(uuid4(), text)
    assert all(chunk.char_count == len(chunk.content) for chunk in chunks)
replace:
import random
    import threading
    import time

    chunks = _service().chunk(uuid4(), text)
    assert all(chunk.char_count == len(chunk.content) for chunk in chunks)

    totals = {"chars": 0}

    def add(batch) -> None:
        time.sleep(random.uniform(0.0, 0.1))
        current = totals["chars"]
        time.sleep(random.uniform(0.0, 0.067))
        totals["chars"] = current + sum(chunk.char_count for chunk in batch)

    halves = [chunks[: len(chunks) // 2], chunks[len(chunks) // 2 :]]
    threads = [threading.Thread(target=add, args=(half,)) for half in halves]
    for thread in threads:
        thread.start()
    for thread in threads:
        thread.join()
    assert totals["chars"] == sum(len(chunk.content) for chunk in chunks)
notes: concurrency: two threads do an unsynchronised read-modify-write on a shared total, each with a random delay before the read and another between read and write. When the two read-write windows overlap, one update is lost and the total comes up short (~50% of runs, set by the ratio of the random delays rather than by CPU speed).
